title: Relative flat extension from a prescribed flat cone replacement
statement: Let E,H be cochain complexes of module sheaves on a small ringed site, and f:E -> H. Assume E has bounded-above flat terms, and prescribe a bounded-above flat complex Q with a quasi-isomorphism r:Q -> Cone(f). There exist a bounded-above flat complex F, maps t:E -> F and g:F -> H, such that g is a quasi-isomorphism and t followed by g equals f strictly. No epimorphy for g is asserted. [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]

proof.text: The prescribed map r:Q -> Cone(f), followed by Cone(f) -> E[1], determines a distinguished triangle E -> F -> Q -> E[1]. Realize F by the shifted cone of this composite; the inclusion E -> F is degreewise split and F^i is isomorphic to E^i plus Q^i. A common bound for E and Q bounds F, and finite coproduct flatness makes its terms flat.

The identity on E and r extend to a morphism from this triangle to the cone triangle E -> H -> Cone(f) -> E[1]. Its middle map g:F -> H is quasi-isomorphic by the long exact cohomology sequences, since identity on E and r are quasi-isomorphisms. The square with E initially commutes up to homotopy. Extend that homotopy to F by precomposing each component with the degreewise retraction F^i -> E^i and subtract its homotopy differential from g. The new g is a chain map, has the same cohomology maps, and satisfies t followed by g equals f strictly.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 06XX (derived-lemma-special-direct-system), induction step; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06XX; separated triangle realization and generalized the source disk addition to every degree below the bound

mathlib_searches.query: relative cone replacement; adding contractible flat disks for termwise epimorphic augmentation

mathlib_searches.results: mappingCone, fst, snd, inl, inr, descCochain, liftCochain and isZero_X_iff; tools for construction, no relative flat extension or flat disk augmentation theorem.

No matching flat relative extension or flat epicification theorem. Mathlib CM5a/CM5b use injectives and lower bounds; unsuitable. Project bounded flat replacements are the existing source of the cone replacement.
